result.markdown: --- title: "[theme_survival()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} A light, publication-ready plotnine theme for survival plots. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/viz/_curves.py#L79-L109){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python theme_survival() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Applies a minimal theme with the legend at the top and minor grid lines removed, giving survival curves a clean look suitable for journal figures. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [plotnine.theme]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A composable theme object. Add it to a `ggplot` with `+`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Apply the survival theme to a Kaplan-Meier plot: ::: {#0f6d6456 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw # Load data and fit a stratified Kaplan-Meier estimator lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") km = gw.KaplanMeier().fit("Surv(time, status) ~ sex", data=lung) # Apply the survival theme to the plot gw.plot_survival(km, backend="plotnine") + gw.theme_survival() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ![](theme_survival_files/figure-html/cell-2-output-1.png){width=672 height=480} ::: :::
